title: Valuation support and prime-factor counts
ant_object: omega(n), distinct-prime support, and radical data
reverse_translation: The labeled support recovers rad(n); omega(n) alone recovers only its cardinality.
preserved_information: prime labels when full support is retained; support size under omega
lost_information: omega discards prime identities, exponents, logarithmic mass, and residue information.
trigger: The problem depends on which primes divide n or on the number of distinct prime factors.
typical_output: support condition, omega-weight, or radical factorization
error_or_wall: A support statistic cannot certify exponent depth or cancellation.
required_certificate: State whether labeled support or only omega is available and identify the theorem controlling its average or distribution.
positive_example: n=360 has support {2,3,5}, omega(n)=3, and rad(n)=30.
counterexample: 12 and 18 have omega=2 but different labeled supports and exponent profiles.
anti_overclaim: Support geometry is an exact encoding, not an asymptotic estimate or originality claim.
source_basis: Unique factorization; classical omega and radical theory

title: Boolean support cube and squarefree projection
forward_translation: Booleanizing nu(n) gives nu(rad(n)); n is squarefree iff every coordinate is 0 or 1.
reverse_translation: rad(n) recovers labeled support but not exponent heights.
preserved_information: which prime coordinates are active and squarefreeness
lost_information: all exponent heights above one and all multiplicity-sensitive weights
trigger: The question separates support from exponent multiplicity or invokes squarefree kernels.
typical_output: squarefree indicator, radical factor, or support-conditioned decomposition
error_or_wall: Boolean projection cannot distinguish powerful numbers sharing the same radical.
required_certificate: Specify whether the argument needs only support or actual exponent heights.
positive_example: nu(72)=(3,2) Booleanizes to (1,1), corresponding to rad(72)=6.
counterexample: 12 and 72 have the same radical 6 but different divisor geometry.
anti_overclaim: The Boolean projection is lossy and cannot support height-dependent conclusions.

title: Coordinate height sums and additive functions
pvg_object: sum over prime coordinates of a local height observable g(p,v_p(n))
ant_object: additive and strongly additive arithmetic functions
forward_translation: F(n)=sum_p g(p,v_p(n)) is additive across coprime products; if g ignores heights above one it is strongly additive.
reverse_translation: An additive function determines local coordinate contributions after fixing its prime-power values.
preserved_information: separable coordinate contributions and coprime additivity
lost_information: interactions between distinct prime coordinates and nonseparable constraints
trigger: The observable is a sum of independent prime-coordinate contributions.
typical_output: mean, variance, normal order, or limiting distribution
error_or_wall: Additive-function models do not capture cross-coordinate coupling without extra terms.
required_certificate: Give the prime-power local function and verify the hypotheses of the selected mean-value or probabilistic theorem.
counterexample: The condition p+q=n is not a separable valuation-coordinate sum.
anti_overclaim: A probabilistic model is not automatically an error term for a deterministic sum.

title: Prime-coordinate logarithmic mass and integer size
pvg_object: weighted linear functional ell(nu)=sum_p v_p(n) log p
ant_object: log n, size cutoffs, and logarithmic weights
forward_translation: ell(nu(n))=log n; n<=x becomes a weighted valuation half-space.
reverse_translation: log n determines only total mass, not the labeled valuation vector.
lost_information: factorization shape, additive order, local spacing, and coordinate distribution
trigger: A multiplicative object is restricted by n<=x, a short interval, or a smooth size weight.
typical_output: weighted lattice region or transform variable
error_or_wall: A half-space picture alone supplies no lattice-counting error or short-interval cancellation.
required_certificate: Name the counting, transform, or Tauberian theorem controlling the boundary.
positive_example: nu(72) has logarithmic mass 3 log 2+2 log 3=log 72.
counterexample: 12 and 18 are close in size but have unrelated valuation directions.
anti_overclaim: Geometric visualization of size is expository until a counting certificate is supplied.

title: Divisor boxes and lattice-point counts
forward_translation: Divisors d|n correspond bijectively to lattice points beta=nu(d) in the divisor box; tau(n)=product_p(v_p(n)+1).
reverse_translation: A labeled divisor box recovers n; tau(n) alone records only box volume in lattice points.
preserved_information: coordinate bounds and exact divisor enumeration
lost_information: tau alone loses dimension, side lengths, labels, and integer ordering of divisors
trigger: The problem sums over d|n or depends on faces, edges, or interiors of the divisor lattice.
typical_output: product formula or coordinatewise divisor count
error_or_wall: Box volume does not determine additive correlations or average-order errors.
required_certificate: Distinguish exact per-integer enumeration from summatory estimates over n.
positive_example: 360=2^3 3^2 5 has a 4x3x2 divisor box and tau(360)=24.
counterexample: 24 and 30 both have small divisor counts but geometrically different boxes.
anti_overclaim: An exact divisor-box identity is not a new average-order theorem.

title: Margin-interior points and weighted powerful support
pvg_object: divisor-box points at coordinate margin at least r from every facet
forward_translation: Interior margin enumeration yields I_r(n)=1_{rad(n)^(2r)|n} tau(n/rad(n)^(2r)).
reverse_translation: The multiplicative weight reconstructs the count but not individual interior divisor locations unless the full box is retained.
preserved_information: margin depth, support threshold, and product count
lost_information: locations of individual interior points and correlations between selected divisors
trigger: The observable excludes boundary layers of a divisor box.
typical_output: weighted k-full Dirichlet series and smoothed asymptotic
error_or_wall: The analytic method is classical; originality and significance require external priority review.
required_certificate: Prove the local Bell series, continuation region, pole data, and the exact transfer hypotheses.
counterexample: A nonzero interior count does not by itself imply equidistribution in residue classes.
anti_overclaim: The internally proved fixed-parameter theorem remains under external originality review.
classification: PVG-derived observable / internally proved application interface
source_basis: One-Theorem Program 001 and classical weighted k-full methods

title: Face enumerators and boundary-coordinate polynomials
pvg_object: number of divisor-box coordinates lying on facets, tracked by a variable z
forward_translation: Each prime coordinate contributes a-1 interior choices of weight 1 and two endpoint choices of weight z.
reverse_translation: The polynomial factors encode side lengths up to permutation; specialization at one z may lose them.
lost_information: prime labels under factor permutation and geometric incidence beyond coordinatewise boundary count
trigger: The question weights divisor points by how many coordinates lie on the boundary.
typical_output: multiplicative face polynomial or z-parametric Dirichlet series
error_or_wall: A formal z-family does not provide uniform analytic continuation in z.
required_certificate: State the z-domain, local factorization, and any uniformity needed before analytic transfer.
counterexample: Phi_1(n)=tau(n) loses the boundary stratification entirely.
anti_overclaim: The polynomial identity is exact; new analytic consequences must be proved separately.
classification: PVG structural family / candidate analytic interface

title: Minimum height constraints and k-full integers
forward_translation: All active valuation coordinates at height at least k iff p|n implies p^k|n.
reverse_translation: The k-full support condition gives a coordinate floor but not the heights above it.
preserved_information: minimum exponent threshold on every active prime
lost_information: excess heights, face location, and weighted multiplicity
trigger: The sequence excludes primes appearing with exponents below a fixed threshold.
typical_output: support restriction and first singular exponent
error_or_wall: A k-full parametrization may be nonunique unless normalization conditions are imposed.
required_certificate: Provide a unique or controlled parametrization and account for bad primes and residue conditions.
positive_example: 72=2^3 3^2 is squarefull because every active exponent is at least 2.
counterexample: 12=2^2 3 is not squarefull despite having the same radical as 72.
anti_overclaim: Support in a classical sparse sequence is not itself a new theorem.
source_basis: Classical powerful and k-full number theory

title: Valuation-vector decompositions and Dirichlet convolution
pvg_object: decompositions beta+gamma=nu(n) inside the valuation lattice
forward_translation: Each divisor split d*(n/d)=n corresponds to a coordinatewise vector split.
reverse_translation: A convolution term recovers the collection of vector decompositions when prime labels are retained.
lost_information: additive decompositions of integers and ordering of factors
trigger: The arithmetic function is defined by a divisor sum or convolution inverse.
typical_output: factorized Dirichlet series or hyperbola decomposition
error_or_wall: Convolution geometry alone does not estimate long bilinear sums.
required_certificate: Specify convergence for transform multiplication or bounds for the chosen hyperbola ranges.
positive_example: tau=1*1, and tau(12)=6 counts six valuation-vector splits.
counterexample: Goldbach decompositions n=p+q are not Dirichlet-convolution decompositions.
anti_overclaim: Multiplicative convolution must not be confused with additive convolution.
